name: 2115 Prairie Avenue — the Kelley/Armour house, a Second Empire stone front (K01; T-3712)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling with a stone front (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'David Kelley-Philip D. Armour Residence. Built 1871'.

research_note: T-3712 (piece 1 of T-1925, the S14 package of the T-1837 programme) refines the district draft (T-2352) in place under its own id: the 1911 sheet's '3B' brick house with a stone front, read at full size, built on K01 to the forms of the Armour photograph (chicagology_2115_armour_photo, forms only) and the Tribune's 1928 'Famous Homes' photograph: a banded stone front of two storeys over a high basement, round-headed keyed lights, the round-arched door at the head of a broad stoop, the south pavilion under its own taller mansard, and a slated, dormered mansard behind iron cresting. The south '2B' piece and the rear '3B' range stand on K08 and K01. Its cameras and the image gate are T-3713's; what the pictures show that this piece has not built is in docs/LIBERTIES.md (L-k01-2115-armour-3712). Philip D. Armour was dead by 1904; no occupancy is assumed for the geometry.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), and the Tribune's photograph shows it standing in 1928. Built 1871 (the marker); its loss is not read here.

position.symbolic_location: 2115 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2115 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The rear corner of the '3B' main body on its north wall (lot frame u 28.63, v -8.66 from the middle of the rear lot line): the main body's rear line at raster column 1017.5 (25.95 m from the street line at column 878) and its north wall at row 1205.5 (0.55 m inside the parcel's north line at row 1202.6), read at full size, 0.186 m a pixel, through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, which carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace. Rotation 179.318 degrees (the draft's) turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The '3B' main body off the 1911 sheet at full size, 0.186 m a pixel: its stone front at raster column 918 (7.44 m from the street line, on 2109's front line), its rear at column 1017.5 (18.51 m deep), its north wall at row 1205.5 and its south wall at row 1273.5 (12.64 m). The sheet's south pavilion (the blue band bowed out about 5 px, rows 1242-1268), its '2B' south piece and its '3B' rear range are K08 projections and a K01 rear wing; the draft's trace (s35fp-2115-b1) had cut the body into a 12.5 m deep block and a 3 m 'bay' in front of it on a coarser copy.

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet: three storeys over a basement, which the Armour photograph shows as two storeys of banded stone wall under the cornice and the mansard's attic over them; K01 counts the walls' storeys, the attic is the mansard's.

construction.note: The sheet colours the street front blue (stone) on a pink (brick) house: '3B brick dwelling with a stone front (D)'. The photograph shows the front's stone banded and quoined and the north flank plain, and the Tribune's 1928 caption calls it 'the old 19-room stone residence'.

stone_front.note: The photograph's front: smooth pale stone laid in bands, deep and shallow courses in turn, over a basement storey in panelled courses. Its tone does not prove the stone (the ticket's phase guard): a smooth Lemont limestone, the avenue's commonest pale stone, is the reconstructed fabric, and K02's alternating coursing stands for the banding; the channels' depth and the quoins' long-and-short are finer than K01 lays here (liberty).

principal_floor_m.note: The stoop's landing at the door: about twelve risers from the walk in the photograph, each taken as 0.18 m (reconstructed).

storey_heights_m.note: The photograph's two storeys of wall, scaled at the door's plane by the stoop's risers, about twelve from the walk to the landing in the photograph (y 1215 to 1035 px, about 15 px a riser), each taken as a 0.18 m riser (reconstructed): about 83 px a metre there: the principal storey from the landing (y 1035) to the belt under the second storey's lights (y 720), about 3.8 m and the belt; the second storey from the belt to the cornice's top (y 415), about 3.7 m with the frieze. T-3713: the second storey carried 0.6 m higher, to 4.5 m, so the wall head stands where the photograph's deep bracketed cornice begins: through the solved camera (data/reference_views/armour_house_2115_prairie/chicagology_armour_photo.json) the cornice runs about 1 m deep at the north corner (y 400-475 px) where K10's moulded stone section is 0.36 m, and the 0.6 m between the second storey's frieze and that section is built as the wall head's frieze with its console blocks (wall_head).

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front on its brick backing, as every K01 stone front.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays.

face_brick.note: The flanks and rear are brick (the sheet's pink); the photograph shows the north flank plain and pale, near the stone's tone (x 520-760 px; paint or a pale brick cannot be told at its scale): K03's buff common brick, the palest the kit lays.

street_front_trim.note: K01's flat stone lintel for any flat-headed light; the front's lights are round-headed (street_front_round_heads), so it lays none.

street_front_round_heads.note: Every front light in both storeys is round-headed in the photograph (x 820-1530, y 540-1035 px), each in a moulded architrave with a carved key, and the door's opening is round-arched under a deep moulded surround; the Tribune's 1928 photograph draws the same round-arched lights.

wall_head.note: The photograph's deep cornice over a frieze of carved panels (y 400-500 px), carried round the north flank (x 380-760); K10's moulded stone cornice, round all four walls (the rear's reconstructed). T-3713: the photograph's cornice is about 1 m deep at the north corner (y 400-475 px through the solved camera), its corona over a close row of consoles about 0.55 m apart (x 670-800 px); K10's section is 0.36 m, so the 0.6 m under it is built as a frieze with K10's console blocks every 0.6 m (as 2100's and 1901's). The consoles' carving and the frieze's panels are finer than K01 lays here (liberty).

roof_form.note: The photograph's slated mansard over the whole house, its steep face carried up from the cornice to a deck behind iron cresting (y 160-420 px), and the Tribune's 1928 photograph's 'tall mansard storey' with round-headed dormers and cresting.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The deck's fall, the K05 mansard's own.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice's projection in the photograph, about half a metre past the frieze at the north corner (x 740-790 px).

mansard.note: The photograph's mansard (y 160-420 px), about 3 m of steep slated face over the cornice scaled at the door's plane by the stoop's risers, about twelve from the walk to the landing in the photograph (y 1215 to 1035 px, about 15 px a riser), each taken as a 0.18 m riser (reconstructed); on the street face a pair of round-headed lights over the two north bays (x 860-1000) and one round-headed dormer over the door (x 1100-1160), each under a carved hood rising to a point; three smaller round-headed dormers on the north flank's face (x 430-570; K01's 'south' face, the house being turned 180 degrees). The pair is built as two K06 round dormers side by side under K01's eared hood, standing for the carved hood rising to a point that they share (liberty); the north face's dormers' places along the face are spaced evenly (reconstructed). Over the south pavilion the photograph's taller mansard crown (x 1220-1440), rising about a metre over the main roof's curb with its own round-headed dormer (x 1340-1390). Round the deck's edge the photograph's iron cresting, about half a metre high (x 770-1220, y 110-160 px), with small finials at its corners, is not built: K01 lays a deck's cresting only where no mansard crown stands on it (liberty). T-3713: its lower rise 3.35 m, the photograph's face from the cornice's top to the deck's curb at the north corner (y 400 to about 180 px, about 220 px where the K05 face rose 195 px through the solved camera at 3.0 m). T-3713: the iron cresting the photograph shows along the deck's curb over the front and the north side (y 120-200 px) is the K10 kit's (k10.cresting.iron_ridge, 0.6 m tall), stopped short of the pavilion's crown either side; its pattern is the kit's, not the print's (liberty). T-3713: the north side's mansard (K01's 'south' face) is plain slate in the photograph from the front's corner back to its first dormer (x 550 px, about 1.5-2 m from the main body's rear through the solved camera), so that side carries one dormer at 2.9 m where T-3712 had three at 5.0, 9.5 and 14.0 m; the dormers the photograph shows further back (x 360-480 px) stand over the rear range (see the match record). T-3713: the crown's own deck carries the photograph's iron cresting round its curb (x 1210-1390, y 160-230 px), the K10 kit's rail at the main deck's 0.6 m (its pattern the kit's, not the print's; liberty), and on its north street corner (K01's street_south) the carved top the photograph draws as a dark block about twice as tall as wide (x 1220-1280, y 120-230 px: about 0.75 m wide and 1.7 m over the crown's curb through the solved camera), and the Tribune's halftone as the ragged top of the crown (y 110-200 px). Its parts — a plinth, a die, a cap and a turned top, all in iron — are K01's, not the carving's, which neither picture resolves (liberty). T-3713 (crown pass): the crown's own deck carries the photograph's iron cresting round its curb (x 1220-1440, y 160-230 px; the Tribune's halftone draws its posts dark against the sky, y 100-130 px), the K10 kit's rail at the main deck's 0.6 m, its pattern the kit's, not the print's (liberty). T-3713 (rear range pass): the north flank's face runs on over the rear range (`rear_wings`) and carries two more of the flank dormer, at -0.55 and -4.0 m along it, as the photograph draws them behind the first (x 360-600 px); their spacing is even, 3.45 m, since the solved camera, fitted on the front, foreshortens the flank more than the print does (liberty).

roof_covering.note: The photograph's mansard faces are slate laid in bands of a darker and a lighter tone in patterns (the register's 'patterned slate'); K04's Pennsylvania slate stands for them in one tone (liberty). The deck behind the cresting is not seen: standing-seam tin (reconstructed).

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A landing a door's swing deep; the photograph sees it edge on.

stoop_width_m.note: The photograph's broad straight flight between solid stone cheeks, a little wider than the door's surround (x 1075-1270 at the landing, about 2.6 m at the door's plane).

entrance_bay.note: The door is the third opening from the north in the photograph's principal storey (x 1085-1180), between the two north bays and the south pavilion: K01 counts a front's bays from its own 'south' end, which on this house, turned 180 degrees, is the real north, so the door is bay 3 (T-3713: T-3712 had set 2, which put the door in the second column with a window south of it, against the photograph's two windows north of the door).

front_bays.note: The photograph's three window columns north of the pavilion (x 820-890, 965-1030 and the door's 1085-1180 px), laid along the front's first 6.9 m from the north corner (x 760) to the pavilion's junction (x 1215), their places read in proportion along that stretch and corrected for its recession (about 0.3 m either way); and (T-3713) the fourth, the front's south end beyond the pavilion, whose one light a storey (x 1475-1525 px, its basement light x 1485-1530) back-projects through the solved camera (data/reference_views/armour_house_2115_prairie/chicagology_armour_photo.json) to about 12.4 m from the north wall, laid at 11.65 m so the light stands clear of the south corner (12.64 m).

north_bays.note: The south flank's lights (K01's 'north' wall, the house being turned 180 degrees); no picture shows that flank.

side_bays.note: T-3713: the photograph's north flank (K01's 'south' wall, the house being turned 180 degrees) is plain stone-pale wall under the cornice from the front corner back to where 2109's veranda and roof hide it (x 520-760 px), but for one tall round-headed light in the second storey (x 555-575, y 630-790 px), which back-projects through the solved camera (data/reference_views/armour_house_2115_prairie/chicagology_armour_photo.json) to 6.4 m from the rear, its sill about 7.2 m and its head about 10 m over grade (laid from 6.8 to 9.2 m, its arch clear of the wall head's frieze and consoles, which start 9.54 m up on this wall: about 0.5 m short of the print's head, within tolerance in the match record): a stair light, laid once at its own place. T-3712 had laid three columns of lights (3.5, 8.0 and 13.0 m) on every storey, two of them on the stretch the photograph shows plain. The flank's hidden rear 2 m carries no light (reconstructed).

rear_bays.note: The rear wall's one light south of the rear range; no picture shows it.

sash_by_storey.note: The photograph's front lights, scaled at the door's plane by the stoop's risers, about twelve from the walk to the landing in the photograph (y 1215 to 1035 px, about 15 px a riser), each taken as a 0.18 m riser (reconstructed): the principal storey's about 2.6 m to the crown of the arch from a sill on the landing's belt (y 1040 to 830 px), the second storey's about 2.2 m (y 715 to 540), each about twice as tall as wide.

basement_lights.note: The photograph's basement lights under the principal lights (x 830-890, y 1090-1190 px), segment-headed in the panelled base; K06's area light with a flat head stands for them, 0.85 m tall where the photograph reads nearer 1.1 m, as tall as K02's two-course rusticated base under its coping allows (liberty).

window_kit.note: K06's two-over-two sash; the round-headed lights' K06 round sash; the area light without a well.

chimneys.note: The photograph's tall carved stack rising from the north side's deck near the front (x 685-745, y 40-200 px) and a second one further back on the same side (x 520-560); the Tribune's 'tall corner stacks'. The third, on the south side, is reconstructed; K01's plain stone stack stands for the carved one (liberty). T-3713: the front stack stands 13.8 m from the rear, where the photograph's (x 685-745 px) back-projects through the solved camera at the north side's 0.85 m (data/reference_views/armour_house_2115_prairie/chicagology_armour_photo.json); T-3712 had it 16.5 m, about 50 px nearer the corner than the print draws it. The second, the photograph's small stack just behind the north side's first dormer (x 520-570 px), back-projects to about the main body's rear and stands 1.4 m from it, clear of the deck's rear curb where the cresting runs (T-3712 had 2.5 m, which the dormer now occupies). Their tops 2.6 m over the deck (T-3712: 1.2 m): the front stack's top stands at y 40 px in the photograph, about 18 m over grade through the solved camera, where 1.2 m put it about 100 px lower; the back one is the same kit stack (the print shows it lower, about 0.5 m over the curb: within tolerance in the match record). The third, on the south side, is no longer reconstructed: the Armour photograph shows its carved top over the pavilion's crown (x 1230-1290, y 110-230 px) and the Tribune's 1928 photograph its 'tall corner stack' at the crown's south end (x about 855 px); triangulated through the two solved cameras (data/reference_views/armour_house_2115_prairie/) it stands about 14.5 m from the rear and 10.4 m from the north wall, its top about 18.5 m up (residuals 2-16 px), where T-3712 had reconstructed it at 9.0 m and 11.8 m. T-3713 (crown pass): the south stack is the tall dark mass both pictures draw over the crown — the Armour photograph's 'carved top' at the crown's north corner (x 1230-1285 px, top y about 120), which its solved camera reaches only from a stack behind the crown, and the Tribune halftone's spike at x about 855 (top y about 105). At the kit's 2.6 m over the deck (17.71 m) it stood about 20 px under the photograph's top and about 40 px under the halftone's, that is about 0.4 m and 1.2 m short through the two cameras; its top_m 18.35 m stands between the two readings (about 0.3 m over the photograph's, about 0.3 m under the halftone's), which disagree by more than the bar (within tolerance in both match records). Its ornamented head, which neither picture resolves beyond a ragged outline, is the kit's plain cap (liberty).

rainwater.note: No picture shows the house's downpipes on the front; one at the rear.

entrance_kit.note: The photograph's door: a pair of leaves under a glazed fanlight in a round-arched opening (x 1085-1180, y 815-1035 px, about 1.4 m by 3.2 m scaled at the door's plane by the stoop's risers, about twelve from the walk to the landing in the photograph (y 1215 to 1035 px, about 15 px a riser), each taken as a 0.18 m riser (reconstructed)) deep in a moulded surround with a carved crest over its arch; K07's deep-arched double door. The surround's carving and the crest are finer than K01 lays here (liberty).

boundary.note: The photograph shows no fence before the house, the yard open to the walk behind a low stone kerb at its edge (y 1220-1290 px), which is not built (liberty). The street line 7.44 m before the front (the sheet's column 878); the lot from its north line, 0.55 m north of the north wall, to its south line 18.40 m on.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the pavilion's basement lights under its principal lights, as the front's (the Armour photograph shows the south one, x 1380-1430 px; the stoop's south cheek hides the north one)
the pavilion's two round-headed principal lights in the Armour photograph (x 1260-1330, 1365-1420 px), sized as the front's
the pavilion's two round-headed second-storey lights in the Armour photograph (x 1250-1315, 1365-1400 px), sized as the front's

bays.note: The south pavilion the 1911 sheet draws on the front: the front's blue band bowed out about 5 px (0.95 m) between rows 1242 and 1268, which the photograph shows as the stretch of the front under its own taller mansard (x 1215-1440 px) with two round-headed lights a storey; the sheet's scalloped edge is built as a square-faced projection (liberty). T-3713: its width is the photograph's, not the sheet's 4.8 m. Through the solved camera (data/reference_views/armour_house_2115_prairie/chicagology_armour_photo.json) its north face stands at the junction x 1215 px and its south corner at x 1440 back-projects to 10.6 m from the north wall, so it is 3.7 m wide with its middle 8.75 m from the north wall; its two lights back-project to 7.96 and 9.7 m (built at 7.96 and 9.75: `at` 0.359 and 0.67 of the bay's 5.6 m run of return, face and return). The sheet's bowed band (rows 1242-1268) reads about a metre wider, its scalloped outline being drawn coarser than the front it stands for; south of the pavilion the front's own wall carries one light a storey (front_bays). The sheet's '2B' south piece (rows 1273.5-1288, 2.7 m past the south wall, columns 921-968) is not built: no K01 part stands a wing beside the main body (liberty).

rear_wings.note: The sheet's '3B' range behind the main body, columns 1017.5-1049 (5.86 m) and rows 1205.5-1255 (9.2 m from the north wall, flush with it). T-3713: the Armour photograph shows the north flank's slated mansard face carried on behind the main body with two more dormers in it (x 360-600 px), so the range is roofed with the house's own mansard (`roof.kind` mansard: the main roof's ring stack carried over it and joined in): two storeys of wall to the main eave, the main body's two, and the sheet's third the mansard's attic. Its rear and south faces are out of the picture (reconstructed).

yard.note: The kit's front yard, open to the walk; the photograph's is under snow, a walk the stoop's width running from its foot to the public walk (y 1220-1260 px).
